### Contributing guidelines

- [X] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

### Module(s)

mini.align

### Question

Is it possible to align by Lua key like this? 

    { on = "<Esc>", run = "escape",             desc = "Exit visual mode, clear selected, or cancel search" },
    { on = "<C-[>", run = "escape",             desc = "Exit visual mode, clear selected, or cancel search" },
    { on = "q",     run = "quit",               desc = "Quit the process" },
    { on = "Q",     run = "quit --no-cwd-file", desc = "Quit the process without outputting cwd-file" },
    { on = "<C-c>", run = "close",              desc = "Close the current tab, or quit if it's last" },
    { on = "<C-z>", run = "suspend",            desc = "Suspend the process" },

Thinking about binding that to a mapping.

Also thinking of a way to move the order of all the keys.

Thanks.

comment_data.body:
The closest approximation here is to align by `,` and press `i` to apply [ignoring common separators](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/a84b7e555fe382c1859e6ca46b4983c822a1f77f/doc/mini-align.txt#L30) (which by default excludes [separators from inside `""` quotes](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/a84b7e555fe382c1859e6ca46b4983c822a1f77f/doc/mini-align.txt#L875-L877)).

> Also thinking of a way to move the order of all the keys.

I usually resort to aligning first and then using [exchange operator](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/a84b7e555fe382c1859e6ca46b4983c822a1f77f/doc/mini-operators.txt#L186-L192) from 'mini.operators' with blockwise visual selections:
- Press `<C-v>` and select the rectangular block for the first key.
- Press `gx`.
- Select rectangular block for the second key.
- Press `gx`.
